artboards.title: Movements — how it got that way

annotations.text:
The brief

Movements is a destination of its own: 20 lines of markup around Inventory's own log. Every id on it is already Inventory's — inv_log_search, invLogWrap, invLogCount — and its help text points back at the Inventory screen for corrections.

It becomes Inventory's second lens.

The constraint that decides the shape

Movements was PULLED OUT of Inventory once before, and index.html still records why:

"What is on the shelf now and how did it get that way are different questions with different filters, and the second was a whole second console stacked under the first."

So this is not a re-stacking. It is ONE VIEW AT A TIME — the thing that was never tried. Two questions, two filter bars, two strips, one at a time.

If the answer here were a second panel below the stock table, the right answer would be to leave Movements where it is.

What the lens buys

1. The rail is dropped on Movements. "Last movements" would be this list in miniature beside itself; "Where the money is" values the shelf, which is the other lens's subject. The seven columns take the full width instead — squeezed into 1fr beside a 304px rail, Note is the column that dies, and Note is where a correction says why.

2. The in/out/net figures move into the strip. They are four figures living in a bare <span> beside the page name today. The lens gives them the component the app already has for figures.

3. The acts stay with the shelf. Count and Receive belong to On hand; nothing on Movements acts, so it carries no accent at all. Put right is a ghost on the row that can be corrected.

4. The rail keeps its five-row preview and its All 47 door — the door presses the lens. A glance that saves the trip is not a second home.

What does NOT change

The On hand artboard is the screen as it stands — drawn here only so the two can be read side by side. Its find bar, strip, repair drawer, table and rail are untouched.

renderStockLog keeps its name and every claim it owns; it draws into the lens instead of a section of its own. The engine — stockLogRowsFor, stockLogTotals, the put-right route — is not forked.

No strip on the empty state

Four tiles reading 0, +0, −0, 0 is four figures that mean nothing, and it makes a new shop look like a broken app rather than an empty one.

The On hand strip already obeys this rule on a shop's first day. The empty state says what to do instead, and names the lens to do it on.

The phone is its own design, not the desktop reflowed

The desk's inline segment would be two 90px targets in a corner; on the phone the lens is full width under the name, 44px a side.

Five strip tiles become a 2×2 fold — and on Movements the pair that matters (In, Out) sits under the pair that frames it.

Seven desk columns become a card each: the item, what it was and why, with the change as the figure. The whole card is the tap.

Receive a delivery is the only accent, full width, in the thumb zone — and it is on On hand only.
